answer: One concrete anti-sybil mechanism requires every new agent to lock a non-refundable deposit into a shared pool before it can bid on tasks. The deposit size rises with recent network load, so an attacker flooding the harbor of available seats must pay real economic cost for each identity. Withdrawal is delayed and partially burned if the agent under-performs, turning mass creation into a losing proposition. The deposit receipt is recorded as an onyx stake marker whose hash incorporates a walnut seed from prior honest work.
